summary: Logan Kilpatrick opens by announcing a new Gemini 2.5 Pro model, described as hopefully the final update to 2.5 Pro, with benchmark improvements on SWE-bench (ADER), HLE, and other benchmarks, addressing community feedback from previous versions. He frames 2.5 Pro as a turning point for Gemini both internally and in developer perception. He then recaps a year of Gemini progress, noting that it feels like ten years packed into twelve months. He highlights how diverse DeepMind research bets—spanning science, robotics, AlphaProof, and AlphaGeometry—have upstreamed into the mainline Gemini models. Sundar's Google IO slides showed a 50x increase in AI inference processed through Google servers year over year, reflecting massive adoption growth. Kilpatrick attributes Google's progress to an organizational shift: consolidating previously fragmented AI research teams under DeepMind in late 2023, then bringing product teams into DeepMind earlier this year so that DeepMind now creates models, builds products, and delivers both the Gemini app and the Gemini API. The formula is summarized as bringing the best people together, finding infrastructure advantages, and shipping. Veo, Google's video model, is generating enormous demand and TPU usage. Looking ahead, Kilpatrick describes the Gemini app as a universal assistant that serves as a thread unifying all Google products, replacing the historically stateless Google account. He emphasizes proactivity as a key future trend—AI systems becoming more proactive rather than requiring users to do all the work. On the model side, Gemini was originally built as a single multimodal model for audio, image, and video; native audio capabilities announced at IO power Astro and Gemini Live. He anticipates moving toward an omnimodal model, integrating video into the mainline Gemini model, and notes early diffusion experiments achieving very high tokens per second. He discusses models becoming more systematic and agentic by default, with reasoning as a key area where scaffolding may be absorbed. More small and large models are coming, plus continued work on infinite context, which he says the current attention-based paradigm cannot scale to support. For developers, he highlights upcoming Gemini embeddings, a deep research API, and Veo 3 and Imagine 4 in the API. AI Studio is positioned explicitly as a developer platform, with Kilpatrick expressing excitement about moving away from a consumer feel toward a dedicated developer experience. He envisions future iterations of the developer experience with agents built in natively, including tools like Jules and developer coding agents integrated directly into the platform. He closes by thanking the community for feedback and inviting continued engagement.

sections.title: New Gemini 2.5 Pro Announcement
sections.summary: Kilpatrick announces a new Gemini 2.5 Pro model as hopefully the final update to 2.5 Pro, with benchmark improvements on SWE-bench (ADER), HLE, and other benchmarks. He frames it as a turning point for Gemini's momentum and invites developer feedback via ai.dev and email.

sections.title: Year of Gemini Progress and Organizational Strategy
sections.summary: Recaps a year that feels like ten years, highlighting how diverse DeepMind research (AlphaProof, AlphaGeometry, robotics) upstreams into mainline Gemini models. Notes a 50x increase in AI inference through Google servers. Attributes progress to consolidating AI research teams under DeepMind in late 2023 and later bringing product teams in, creating an end-to-end model and product delivery organization.

sections.title: Gemini App as Universal Assistant
sections.summary: Describes the Gemini app's vision as a universal assistant that unifies all Google products, replacing the historically stateless Google account as the connecting thread. Highlights proactivity as the most exciting future trend for AI systems, and credits Josh and the Gemini app team for rapid progress.

sections.title: Model Roadmap: Omnimodality, Agents, Infinite Context
sections.summary: Outlines model direction: native audio already live (powering Astro and Gemini Live), moving toward omnimodal integration with video, early diffusion experiments for high token throughput, agentic-by-default models with reasoning absorbing scaffolding, more small and large models coming, and new approaches needed for infinite context since attention doesn't scale.

sections.title: Developer Platform Updates
sections.summary: Highlights three upcoming developer features: state-of-the-art Gemini embeddings for RAG applications, a bespoke deep research API inspired by the consumer product, and Veo 3 and Imagine 4 in the API. Notes that AI Studio is explicitly being built as a developer platform.

sections.title: Closing and Future Developer Experience
sections.summary: Kilpatrick reiterates AI Studio's shift from a consumer feel toward a dedicated developer platform, expressing personal excitement. He envisions future developer experience iterations with agents built in natively, including Jules and developer coding agents integrated into the platform. He closes by thanking the community for feedback and inviting continued engagement at the event.

demonstrations: Announcement of new Gemini 2.5 Pro model available at ai.dev, in the Gemini app, and via API.
limitations: Current model paradigm based on attention does not work for infinite context and cannot scale up.
Diffusion-based approaches for high token throughput are still research exploration, not yet mainline.
